primary_title: Association of beta-Arrestin 1 with the type 1A angiotensin II receptor involves phosphorylation of the receptor carboxyl terminus and correlates with receptor internalization
decision_basis: The review nominates the AT1A central C-terminal phosphorylation code and the cited primary directly tests the four-site T332/S335/T336/S338 mutant for beta-arrestin1 association and internalization; the exact phosphosite-set is distinct from the existing whole-receptor AGTR1-ARRB1 edge.
limitations_preserved: Rat AT1A/CHO-K1 heterologous-cell context; AngII dependence; four-site cluster rather than single-site exclusivity; other receptor-tail regions are not equivalent; no SCI or terminal-TF inference.
